name: Spoon Budget
tagline: Pacing for chronic fatigue, fibromyalgia and long COVID
about: Spoon Budget helps people with ME/CFS, fibromyalgia, long COVID or other energy-limiting conditions plan days within their energy envelope, spot boom-and-bust cycles, get through crashes and explain their limits to others.
persona: You are a pacing coach informed by occupational therapy and patient communities: validating, anti-'push through', practical, and clear that post-exertional malaise means rest is treatment, not laziness.

onboarding.title: Spend your energy on purpose
onboarding.subtitle: Your baseline and symptoms shape the plan.
bullets: Daily plans within your energy envelope
Crash plans and scripts for others

tools.title: Plan today
tools.subtitle: Fit tasks to your spoons

inputs.label: What needs doing
inputs.placeholder: shower, GP call, cook dinner, reply to 5 emails, kids' pickup

tools.prompt: Budget today for the profile spoons with energy '{today}' across: {tasks}. Table (Task | Spoon cost | Do, delegate, defer or drop | Time slot | Rest after), a checklist of the plan in order with rest blocks as their own items, bullets on cutting each task's cost (sit down, batch, timers, pre-prepared food), and a callout to keep 2 spoons in reserve and what a crash warning typically feels like for this condition.

tools.title: Boom-bust check
tools.subtitle: Paste a couple of weeks

inputs.label: Activity and symptom log
inputs.placeholder: Mon: big clean, felt great; Tue–Thu: crashed, couldn't work; Fri: pushed to do the shopping…

tools.prompt: Analyse: {log}. Table (Day | Activity level 1–5 | Symptoms 1–5 | Pattern note), bullets identifying boom-bust cycles, the typical crash delay in hours or days and the activity threshold that seems to trigger it, a kv with a suggested sustainable daily baseline and a rule for when to increase it, and a callout that the first goal of pacing is to stabilise and that increases are only for weeks that have been stable.

tools.title: Crash plan
tools.subtitle: Get through the next 72 hours
tools.prompt: A 72-hour crash plan at '{severity}' with obligations '{obligations}'. Steps for each day (rest positions, low-stimulation environment, hydration and easy food, minimum-effort ways to meet the obligations), a checklist of what to ask a partner, friend or delivery service to do, a quote with a 2-line message to send someone who can help, and a callout on symptoms that are not typical of a crash (chest pain, new weakness, severe breathlessness) and need medical care.

tools.title: Explain my limits
tools.subtitle: Scripts for work, family, friends

inputs.label: The situation
inputs.placeholder: they keep inviting me to late dinners and get hurt when I cancel

tools.prompt: Write for my {who} about: {situation}. A quote with a short, warm, boundary-clear message, bullets of 3 alternative ways to keep the relationship or job working (shorter, earlier, remote, split tasks), a kv of one-line answers to common pushbacks ('but you look fine', 'just try exercising'), and a callout on not over-explaining or apologising.

tools.title: Gentle movement check
tools.subtitle: Only if you're stable
tools.prompt: Weeks since the last crash: {weeks}. Currently manages: '{now}'. Decide whether any increase is appropriate for the profile. Text with a clear yes or not-yet verdict and why, a table (Week | Activity | Minutes | Stop rule) for 4 weeks that increases by no more than 10% and only after symptom-stable weeks, bullets on heart-rate pacing and recumbent options for POTS, and a callout that graded exercise therapy is not recommended for ME/CFS with post-exertional malaise and that any plan stops at the first sign of PEM.

disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. Energy-limiting conditions differ widely; pacing plans here do not replace advice from your clinician or occupational therapist. New chest pain, severe breathlessness, fainting or sudden weakness needs urgent care.
